description: Captures two seconds of sound and weaves it into a loop of short fragments, a brand new loop every time the big knob moves, with three strands of fragments that each have a level and a gate output

params.text: The loom: at the far anticlockwise end it erases the sample and stops, entering the low zone starts a two-second capture, and anywhere above that any movement weaves a completely new loop
Sets the level of the long, sparse foundation strands, and with it the level of their delay tail
Sets the level of the medium strands crossing them, and with it the level of their delay tail
Sets the level of the shorter, brighter accents an octave up, and with it the level of their delay tail
Chooses whether the fragments are long overlapping smears or short percussive pieces; flipping it re-renders the weave in the new setting rather than making a new one
Chooses whether the fragments are shifted by sympathetic intervals, octaves, fifths and fourths, or by whole semitones picked at random
Starts a two-second capture without stopping the loop; the new sound replaces the old inside the weave that is already running

inputs.text: A rising edge through 1V starts a two-second capture
Weaves a new loop on any change of voltage here, in place of moving the knob
Paces the loom's steps in place of the weave's own tempo

outputs.text: The left side of the woven loop
The right side of the woven loop
A gate at every firing of the long, sparse strands; it fires even with nothing recorded
A gate at every firing of the medium strands; it fires even with nothing recorded
A gate at every firing of the bright accents; it fires even with nothing recorded

notes: the three gate outputs fire whether or not anything is recorded, so this doubles as a random rhythm generator on its own.
the sample is not saved with the patch. Only the weave's seed survives a reload, so reopening a patch gives the same loop structure with nothing in it until something is recorded again.
every weave rolls its own tempo, between about 45ms and 300ms a step, so a loop of about sixteen steps runs between roughly 0.7 and 4.8 seconds.
menu: Restart loop on every weave — makes each new weave start from the beginning of its loop rather than carrying on from where the old one had reached
Loop evolution — how far a weave drifts as it repeats: Frozen, which repeats it exactly, Slow, where a strand changes about once a minute, or Fast, the drift measured in the maker's recordings
Declick — fades the fragment edges to keep the joins from clicking

inputs.1:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.3:
high above 1V · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
